note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Pastor Philip Anthony Mitchell preached that black people use their ethnicity as an idol, that black people don't like white people for something they cannot control, and that Ephesians 2 is about joining blacks and whites together through Christ into one family. Did he forget about slavery? He leans on Ephesians 2:14: “For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” So we have to deal with the us. Who is Paul talking about?

Paul uses two specific words, our and us. To know who they are, go back to the top of the letter and see who it was written to: “Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus, and to the faithful in Christ Jesus.”

The letter was written to the saints which are at Ephesus. So the question becomes, who are the saints according to the holy scriptures? Answer that, and you know who the our and the us are in chapter 2. It is not blacks and whites coming together.

Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”. When they try to hem you up with Ephesians 2, before you get to Ephesians 2 you have to deal with Ephesians 1 and 1: who are the saints he is addressing? The Psalms answer it.

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The saints are the children of Israel, a people near unto him. They are the only saints.

There are no saints called Catholics, no saints called Baptists, Methodists or Presbyterians. Taking the name of saints away from Israel and giving it to the churches is supersessionism, replacement theology. So everything that follows in Ephesians 1, the spiritual blessings in heavenly places, the choosing before the foundation of the world, the adoption, the redemption through his blood, is spoken to the saints, and the saints are Israel.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians explains how Christ “spoiled principalities and powers”: it is the power “Which he wrought in Christ, when he raised him from the dead, and set him at his own right hand in the heavenly places, Far above all principality, and power, and might, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this world, but also in that which is to come.”

Why is that so heavy? Everybody argues about the name. Not only does Christ have a name above everything now; even in the world to come he is going to have a name above every name. Nobody is going to have his name. You have a million men named Jesus running through Puerto Rico; who is that?

“And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.” Christ is the head over all things to the church, and the church is his body.

So back in Colossians: he was not supposed to come back, but with the power of God, being the creator, he rose from the dead and overcame all death. “He made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.” Everybody saw him come from the grave; over five hundred people saw Christ at one time. That is the triumph over the principalities and powers, and it sets him far above every one of them.

precepts.point: For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body. A video of a church baptism in a filthy pond was shown, and the teachers had some fun with it, but this verse is not talking about getting dunked in water. Baptized means cleanse; write that down and look it up yourself. Baptized does not automatically mean dipped in water; that is what a lot of Southern Baptists think.

note.label: Members of the Body  Pt2

precepts.why:
“so also is Christ”. How is the body Christ? Ephesians: “And hath put all things under his feet, and gave him to be the head over all things to the church, Which is his body, the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

God put all things under Christ's feet and gave him to be the head over all things to the church. Who is the head? Christ. Who is the body? The church. And who is the church? Us.

So when Paul says the many members are one body, “so also is Christ”, he means that we, the members, are his body, and he is the head over all of it. That is why there can be no division in the body: every member belongs to the same head, and the body is “the fulness of him that filleth all in all.”

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Paul writes “to the saints which are at Ephesus”, the same saints as at Rome. Who are the saints? “Gather my saints together unto me; those that have made a covenant with me by sacrifice.” No other nation made a covenant with God by sacrifice.

“According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world”. As Eve was in Adam, we the bride were in Christ, chosen before the world was founded, “that we should be holy and without blame before him in love”.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. The adoption is the reconciliation, the atonement, the justification and the restoration.

So the many made righteous by the obedience of one in Romans 5 are the saints God chose in Christ before the foundation of the world. Adam’s offence brought death on the chosen line, and Christ’s obedience brings them back into the adoption that was always theirs.

“Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will”. To be predestinated means you are going to get it no matter what. The definition read was: of an outcome or course of events determined in advance by divine will or fate, with the synonyms preordained, foreordained, destined, predetermined, fated, predestined.

How do you know who is predestined? You don't. Nobody today knows it. When you make it to the kingdom, that is how you know you were predestined. Read on: “To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.”

When were we predestined? When God chose to separate the light from the darkness, on the first day. Revelation 13:8 says the same thing from the other side: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.” When was your name written in the book of life? From the foundation of the world. The choosing was done in the beginning, before the earth was made.
